subject: LumenPay inference disruption — summary, timeline, and compensation path
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared@lumenpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenPay Support <support@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors affecting payments (token truncation)

Hi Rishi,

We saw a spike in failed payment authorizations this morning between 08:45–09:05 PDT. Calls to /v1/generate returned truncated responses (cut off mid-token) and our gateway classified them as malformed, which caused ~0.6% of live transactions to fail.

Example (request id included):
- request_id: lp-req-77321
- model: open-redwood-1.0
- client_timestamp: 2028-05-09T08:47:12Z
- error: truncated output after 120 tokens

This is impacting our reconciliation and we need a clear timeline and remediation/compensation plan. Please advise what caused this and what you will do to prevent recurrence.

We are preparing a short summary for ops and legal — would appreciate a response within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Jared
VP, Payments Engineering
LumenPay

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors affecting payments (token truncation)

Hi Jared — thanks for the report and the example. I'm escalating to engineering now and will lead the customer communication.

Immediate notes:
- We've opened internal ticket RED-8342 and are pulling server-side traces for the request ids you included.
- Initial mitigation: we temporarily pinned LumenPay traffic to a stable model variant and increased stream buffering to avoid partial flushes. That should prevent further truncated responses while we investigate.
- ETA for preliminary findings: ~24–48 hours.

I'll follow up with a concise incident summary (timeline, root findings, and actions) and a proposal for credits/compensation. Grace will coordinate any billing adjustments and Stephanie will drive the engineering fix.

Appreciate the patience — we'll get you a full write-up by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-10T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft customer summary — timeline + actions (internal)

Rishi / Stephanie — drafting below and proposing we send to Jared + ops today. Feedback inline.

Draft customer-facing summary (concise):
1) What happened (summary): Between 08:42–09:02 PDT on 2028-05-09 a subset of generation requests experienced premature stream termination resulting in truncated outputs. Impact: ~0.6% of LumenPay live transactions blocked.

2) Why it happened (root findings):
- Regression in our scheduler that, under a specific concurrent sequence pattern produced by LumenPay traffic, disabled an internal backpressure path when combined with a new continuous-batching kernel change.
- This produced an edge case where the streaming buffer was flushed before KV cache population completed for requests hitting a warmup boundary, causing partial token emission.
- Contributing factor: an incomplete integrity check in the streaming path that would have detected truncated frames.

3) Timeline (high level):
- 2028-05-09 08:42 PDT — first anomalous traces observed by LumenPay
- 08:47 — LumenPay reports truncated output (request lp-req-77321)
- 08:50 — Redwood alert threshold for truncated-frames breached; autoscaler initiated burst policy
- 08:52 — Scheduler regression surfaced in traces; workaround applied (traffic pinned to stable variant)
- 09:05 — No new truncated responses observed for pinned traffic

4) Immediate actions taken:
- Pinned LumenPay to stable model variant and increased stream buffering (mitigation completed 08:52 PDT)
- Rolled back the batch-kernel optimization for affected pools
- Enabled additional integrity checks to detect truncated frames and alert earlier

5) Planned next actions (owner and ETA):
- Engineering (Stephanie): deliver and deploy a permanent fix to the scheduler and kernel selection logic — ETA 2028-05-11 EOD (post-testing)
- Platform (Grace): add synthetic traffic tests for LumenPay-like sequence patterns and expand monitoring thresholds — ETA 2028-05-18
- Customer success (Rishi): propose billing compensation and confirm verification steps with LumenPay — Rishi to send proposal today

6) Proposed customer compensation:
- One month of usage credit prorated to the impacted volume, plus a one-time billing credit for reconciliation effort; additional dedicated capacity consult offered at no charge.

7) Attachments for audit: incident-timeline.csv, patch-diff.patch, and internal traces (referenced).

Please review and flag any technical inaccuracies. Stephanie — confirm the ETA for the patch and whether we can move that to 05/10 with a staged rollout.

Thanks,
Grace

---
Attachment: incident-timeline.csv; patch-diff.patch

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared@lumenpay.com>, LumenPay Support <support@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: LumenPay inference disruption — summary, timeline, and customer recovery plan

Hi Jared — following up with the full accountability summary and our concrete recovery steps. Apologies again for the disruption and the downstream impact to your payments flow. Below is a concise, customer-friendly RCA and next steps.

Executive summary:
- What happened: the platform emitted truncated streaming responses for a subset of LumenPay requests during a 20-minute window (08:42–09:02 PDT on 2028-05-09). This prevented ~0.6% of transactions from completing.
- Root cause: a scheduler regression combined with a recent batching/kernel optimization produced a race where streaming buffers could flush before KV cache completion for certain sequence patterns.
- Immediate mitigation: we pinned LumenPay traffic to a known-good model variant and increased stream buffering; truncated responses stopped for pinned traffic by 08:52 PDT.

Technical timeline (high level):
- 08:42 PDT — anomalous traces begin for LumenPay shard
- 08:47 PDT — LumenPay reports truncated response (lp-req-77321)
- 08:50 PDT — alert threshold exceeded; platform initiates burst autoscaling
- 08:52 PDT — mitigation (variant pin + buffering) applied; truncated responses cease for pinned traffic
- 09:05 PDT — monitoring confirms stability for all LumenPay routes

What we changed (short-term and permanent):
- Short-term (already applied): variant pinning, buffer increase, rollback of the affected kernel change.
- Permanent (in progress): patch to scheduler/kernel selection (testing complete, patch queued for staged deployment), integrity checks in streaming path to detect truncated frames earlier, and expanded synthetic tests for your request shape.

Proposed timeline & owner:
- 2028-05-11 — customer-facing summary delivered (this email) — Rishi
- 2028-05-11 EOD — engineering deploys scheduler fix to canary and begins staged rollout — Stephanie
- 2028-05-18 — monitoring for synthetic patterns expanded and verification complete — Grace

Compensation proposal:
- A prorated one-month usage credit covering the impacted request volume, plus a one-time $2,000 credit toward reconciliation costs. If you prefer, we can convert the credit into a discounted dedicated capacity consult. Grace will coordinate billing details.

Verification and next steps for you:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether the example request lp-req-77321 now returns normal output for your replay test.
2) If you want us to run a targeted verification window from your end, tell us the time and we will prewarm and monitor in real time.
3) Grace will follow up separately on the billing adjustment and send a short statement you can use for your internal post-incident report.

We take incidents like this seriously. Attached is a short PDF summary for your records (customer-summary-20280511.pdf) and supporting artifacts for audit. If you'd like a call to walk through the timeline with our engineering lead, we can be available this week.

Thanks for working through this with us — and again, apologies for the impact.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
